title: Horizontal curve models and schematic closures of markings
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. The scheme $X$ is reduced and has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. If $q:Y\to X$ is a reduced modification, then $Y$ is a $T$-curve and $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism. The schematic closure $E$ of $D_\eta$ in $Y$ makes $(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves, and $E$ is the unique flat closed subscheme of $Y$ with this prescribed generic fibre. More generally, if $Y$ is an integral $T$-curve and $q:Y\to X$ is a birational quasi-modification which identifies $Y_\eta$ with an open of $X_\eta$, the schematic closure in $Y$ of $D_\eta\cap Y_\eta$ is flat and finitely presented over $T$ of pure relative dimension zero. These closure constructions commute with restriction to quasi-compact open subschemes of $Y$. The same assertions apply to a curve without markings by taking $D$ empty. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with that of one irreducible component of the reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W$ of its function field, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ inducing the generic-point map. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$.  A modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens of source and target. The schematic closure of a generic closed subscheme is defined on an affine open by the kernel of the restriction map to its generic-fibre quotient ring.

proof.text: On an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ over an affine chart of $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$, flatness over the domain $V$ makes $A\to A\otimes_VK$ injective. The generic fibre is smooth over the field $K$, hence reduced, so every such $A$ is reduced. Flatness also makes the generic point of every irreducible component specialize from the generic fibre; therefore the generic fibre meets every component. A finite affine cover of the finitely presented scheme $X$ and the finite-type $K$-scheme $X_\eta$ then show that $X$ has finitely many irreducible components. This proves the first assertion, including the empty case.

source.place: Remark 4.1, pp. 24--25; flatness and generic-fibre reduction argument in the opening of §4.2, p. 26

proof.text:
Let $q:Y	o X$ be a reduced modification, inducing an isomorphism $U\xrightarrow{\sim}U'$ between schematically dense opens $U\subseteq Y$, $U'\subseteq X$. $Y$ is of finite type over $T$ ($q$ proper, $X	o T$ finitely presented), so the underlying space of an affine open of $Y$ is the union of its finitely many fibres over the finite space $T$, each Noetherian; hence $Y$ is a quasi-compact Noetherian space with finitely many irreducible components. If the generic point $\xi$ of a component $C$ were not in $U$, the nonempty open $V'$ of points of $Y$ on no other component lies in $C$, and $V'\cap U$ is an open of the irreducible $C$ missing its generic point, hence empty; then $\mathcal O_Y(V')
eq0$ maps to $(j_*\mathcal O_U)(V')=0$, contradicting schematic density. So every generic point of $Y$ lies in $U$ and maps to a generic point of $X$, which lies in $X_\eta$ by Step 1; distinct generic points of $Y$ have distinct images. Generic fibre: by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal] applied to the smooth ring maps $K	o\mathcal O(W)$ ($K$ a field is a normal ring), every local ring of $X_\eta$ is a normal domain; in particular a point lies on only one irreducible component, so $X_\eta$ is covered by integral affine opens $W$. Fix such $W$. Its preimage $E=q^{-1}(W)\subseteq Y_\eta$ is reduced, its generic points are generic points of $Y$ mapping injectively to the single generic point of $W$, and $E
eq\varnothing$ since $W\cap U'
eq\varnothing$; hence $E$ is integral, and $U\cap E\cong U'\cap W$ makes $E	o W$ dominant with $k(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(E)$. $E	o W$ is proper, so $E$ is separated and of finite type over $K$; by [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg], $\dim E=\operatorname{trdeg}_Kk(E)=\operatorname{trdeg}_Kk(W)=\dim W=1$, the last since $X_\eta$ has pure dimension one. Now [lem-trf-proper-birational-normal-curve-iso] shows $E	o W$ is an isomorphism; these glue, so $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism. Flatness: every local ring of the reduced scheme $Y$ injects into the product of its localizations at minimal primes, which are local rings of $Y$ at generic points, hence $K$-algebras; so multiplication by every nonzero element of $V$ is injective on the coordinate rings of affine opens of $Y$, and [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] gives flatness of $Y	o T$. The morphism $q$ is proper, hence of finite type and separated, and $X	o T$ is of finite presentation, so $Y	o T$ is of finite type and quasi-separated. Finite presentation: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ choose a surjection $P=V[x_1,\dots,x_n]	o B$ and regard $\mathcal F=\widetilde B$ as a finite-type quasi-coherent module on $\mathbf A^n_T$, flat over $T$. Its restriction to $\mathbf A^n_K$ is $B\otimes_VK$, a finite module over the Noetherian ring $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, hence finitely presented. The open $\{\eta\}=D(a)$ for any nonzero $a$ in the height-one prime of the finite chain is quasi-compact in the affine $T$, hence retrocompact, and scheme-theoretically dense because $V$ injects into its localizations. [lem-trf-flat-finite-type-dense-presentation] for $\mathbf A^n_T	o T$ shows that $B$ is a finitely presented $P$-module, so the kernel of $P	o B$ is a finitely generated ideal (from $0	o I	o P	o B	o0$ with $P$ finite free and $B$ finitely presented); thus $Y	o T$ is of finite presentation. Finally $Y_\eta\cong X_\eta$ is dense in $Y$ (it contains all generic points) with components of dimension one, and [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] gives pure dimension one for every nonempty fibre and geometric fibre. Thus $Y$ is a $T$-curve.

source.place: Remark 4.1, pp. 24--25; Lemma 3.5.1, p. 20 (torsion-freeness, flatness and finite presentation)

proof.text: For the marking, work on an affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$ and write $I_\eta$ for the ideal in $B\otimes_VK$ of the generic marking, transported to $Y_\eta$ by the isomorphism $q_\eta$ of Step 2. Define the schematic closure by $I=\ker(B\to(B\otimes_VK)/I_\eta)$. Then $B/I$ injects into the $K$-vector space $(B\otimes_VK)/I_\eta$; hence $B/I$ is torsion-free, and [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] makes it flat over $V$. Finite presentation: apply [lem-trf-flat-finite-type-dense-presentation] to the locally finitely presented $Y\to T$ (Step 2), the finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal O_E$ (flat over $T$), and the retrocompact scheme-theoretically dense open $\{\eta\}\subseteq T$ of Step 2; over $\eta$ it is $\mathcal O_{E_\eta}$, finitely presented on the locally Noetherian $Y_\eta$. Hence $\mathcal O_E$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal O_Y$-module, so the ideal $I$ is finitely generated and $E\to Y\to T$ is of finite presentation. (No finiteness of $E$ over $T$ is claimed: the closure algebra need not be a finite $V$-module.) Its generic fibre $E_\eta\cong D_\eta$ is etale over $K$ of dimension zero, and it is dense in $E$ because $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_E\otimes_VK$ is injective; [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] gives pure relative dimension zero. The closed immersion $E\hookrightarrow Y$ followed by the proper map $q$ factors through $D\hookrightarrow X$: the pullback of the ideal of $D$ vanishes on the generic fibre of $E$, and the flat $V$-module $\mathcal O_E$ is torsion-free, so that ideal pullback is zero. Thus $E\to D$ is proper ($E\to X$ is proper and $D\to X$ is separated). Over the open $D_\eta$ of $D$ (open because $\{\eta\}$ is open in $T$, schematically dense because $D$ is flat over the domain $V$), and on generic fibres, $E\to D$ is the prescribed isomorphism $E_\eta\cong D_\eta$; likewise $q$ is an isomorphism over the schematically dense open $X_\eta$ by Step 2. So the pair map is an $\eta$-modification. The empty marking gives $E=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1, p. 20; opening paragraph of §4.2, p. 26

proof.text: The closure is the unique flat closed subscheme with this generic fibre. Indeed, if $F$ is another flat closed subscheme with ideal $J$, then flatness over the domain $V$ gives $B/J\hookrightarrow(B/J)\otimes_VK$. Equality of the generic fibres says that $I$ and $J$ have the same images in $B\otimes_VK$, so the two kernels $\ker(B\to(B\otimes_VK)/I_\eta)$ and $\ker(B\to(B\otimes_VK)/J_\eta)$ coincide. This proves $I=J$ on every affine chart, hence $E=F$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1, p. 20 (uniqueness of the flat closure)

proof.text: If $W\subseteq Y$ is quasi-compact open, the same kernel formula computes the closure on each affine chart of $W$. Restriction only localizes $B$ and $B\otimes_VK$, and localization commutes with the displayed kernel because the localization map is exact. Therefore the closure in $W$ is the restriction of $E$, and the same holds for all quasi-compact restrictions.

Finally let $Y$ be an integral $T$-curve and let $q:Y\to X$ be a birational quasi-modification identifying $Y_\eta$ with an open of $X_\eta$. Replace $D_\eta$ by its intersection with that open, an open subscheme of the etale zero-dimensional $D_\eta$, and repeat the affine kernel construction of Step 3. The closure algebra $B/I$ injects into the $K$-vector space $(B\otimes_VK)/I_\eta$, so it is torsion-free over $V$, and [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] gives flatness. Since $Y\to T$ is locally of finite presentation and $\{\eta\}\subseteq T$ is retrocompact and scheme-theoretically dense by finite height, [lem-trf-flat-finite-type-dense-presentation] applied to the finite-type flat $\mathcal O_Y$-module of the closure, whose generic restriction is finitely presented on the locally Noetherian $Y_\eta$, shows that the ideal is finitely generated, so the closure is finitely presented over $T$. Its generic fibre is the zero-dimensional scheme $D_\eta\cap Y_\eta$, dense in the closure by flatness, so [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] gives pure relative dimension zero. The localization argument of Step 5 proves compatibility with quasi-compact restrictions. Taking $D=\varnothing$ makes every generic marking and every closure empty, proving the unmarked case.
